scope: Tracked repository layout and planning documents
Desktop, website and extension npm lockfiles
Both Rust lockfiles queried against OSV/RustSec
Installer asset selection and platform refusal
Signed updater dependency features and Windows ZIP extraction
Account-file permission helpers, T3 profile guards, Tauri capability boundary and website issue-handler controls
changes: Upgraded Next.js16.3.8 to16.4.5; npm audit now reports zero findings in next,tauri,extension.
Compatible desktop build/test lockfile refresh, including Vite,Vitest and transitive audit fixes.
Patched Rustls0.23.46, rustls-webpki0.103.16, webpki-root-certs1.0.10, ctutils0.4.4 and Tokio1.53.3 across applicable locks.
Disabled the legacy ZIP updater feature on Windows/Linux; Mac alone enables archive support. Windows continues receiving signed raw EXE.
Moved three working plans out of tracked source; retained public historical release evidence and Git history. Added repository ownership guidance and a guard against tracking private notes.
Preserved canonical /install; repaired shell-installer errors that referred to removed README commands.

disposition.glib: RUSTSEC-2024-0429 concerns VariantStrIter. Existing GTK0.18/Tauri stack requires glib0.18; no direct use of the affected iterator was found in this project. A platform-stack migration is not included, and this remains an upstream advisory rather than a clean Rust audit.
disposition.zip: The lockfile still resolves cross-target optional ZIP dependencies. Windows dependency-tree inspection finds no zip package after disabling that target feature. Raw EXE updater acceptance/refusal must pass on the native runner. Mac uses tar archive support, not the Windows ZIP extraction path.
disposition.maintenance: proc-macro-error, UNIC and zbus/zvariant ecosystem maintenance warnings remain. Unmaintained packages are recorded, not treated as proof of an exploitable attack.

verification.windowsZipDependencyTree: no zip package in selected Windows target

limitations: This is a focused code/dependency review, not a penetration test or a guarantee that no unknown vulnerabilities exist.
No evidence of exploitation established. Advisory impact depends on deployed features and inputs.
The npm CLI wrapper has no lockfile and only optional native platform packages; no npm audit result is claimed for that wrapper.
No real account credentials/chats/environment files were used as test fixtures.
